subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should this TUI issue be solved as a renderer-only scrollback/jump repair, a user-visible TUI auto-follow mode or setting, or both?
rationale: Source inspection supports a credible TUI rendering path, but default terminal follow behavior and any persisted setting affect user experience and configuration surface beyond a narrow bug patch.

options.title: Set TUI anchoring policy plus visible control
options.body: Add a TUI-owned near-bottom/off/always or equivalent mode, keep browser WebChat settings separate, and require live PTY proof for streaming and follow-up sends.

options.title: Repair only the renderer jump path
options.body: Patch the pi-tui/OpenClaw render path to avoid disruptive redraws without adding a user-facing preference yet.

options.title: Resolve narrower scrollback loss first
options.body: Use the open long-message scrollback issue as the first concrete fix target, then revisit this broader auto-follow request after live proof.

recommendation.title: Set TUI anchoring policy plus visible control
recommendation.body: Add a TUI-owned near-bottom/off/always or equivalent mode, keep browser WebChat settings separate, and require live PTY proof for streaming and follow-up sends.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and history put Peter closest to the current TUI update path and the product-level decision about default terminal behavior.
